newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese president to head Timor group in Lisbon.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese president to head Timor group in Lisbon.

text.p: Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio has said he would accept an offer to head a foundation to support East Timor's independence cause to be created by Nobel laureate Jose Ramos-Horta.
"For me it will be a great honour to be patron of this foundation that Jose Ramos-Horta plans to establish in Lisbon," Sampaio said at a dinner to honour Ramos-Horta late on Monday.
Ramos-Horta said on Monday he would devote his share of $1.12 million from this year's Nobel peace prize to set up the foundation to support the territory's independence cause.
He said the Lisbon-based foundation, which would accept funds from other sources, would provide financial support to East Timorese widows, orphans and prisoners.
Ramos-Horta shared the award with the Bishop of Timor Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo.
They received the prize for their work to find a peaceful solution to the conflict in East Timor which has been in turmoil since Indonesia invaded it in 1975.
The United Nations does not recognise Indonesian sovereignty and considers Portugal, the former colonial power, as the administering power.
